target.title: fix(agents): preserve runtime tool inheritance tokens for spawned subagents (#85030)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #85030: MCP/LSP/plugin tools not injected into subagent (sessions_spawn) sessions.

Deferred runtime selectors (`bundle-mcp`, `server__tool`, `lsp_*`, `group:plugins`) materialize into concrete tools only at runtime (MCP servers connect async, LSP/plugin tools build lazily). When a spawned subagent inherits the parent's effective tool surface via `replaceWithEffectiveToolAllowlist`, these selectors were absent from the synchronous concrete parent tool array and were silently dropped. The child then received only built-in tools, breaking multi-agent orchestration where worker agents need MCP/LSP/plugin tools.

### Root Cause

In all three spawn paths (`createOpenClawCodingTools`, `resolveGatewayScopedTools`, `resolveSkillDispatchTools`), the inherited allowlist was populated exclusively from concrete parent tools. Deferred selectors like `bundle-mcp` or `probe__search` have no concrete tool counterpart in the synchronous tool array, so they were dropped — even though the parent's policy explicitly authorized them.

### Fix

1. **Identify** deferred selectors with `isRuntimeMaterializationAllowlistEntry`
2. **Expand** each selector to its umbrella policy names (e.g. `probe__search` → `[probe__search, bundle-mcp, group:plugins]`)
3. **Re-filter** them through the SAME ordered authorization layers that produced the concrete parent tool set — security guarantee: a child can never gain a runtime the parent's policy denies
4. **Preserve** surviving tokens via a new `preserveRuntimeToolAllowlistEntries` option on `replaceWithEffectiveToolAllowlist`

Applied in three code paths: `createOpenClawCodingTools`, `resolveGatewayScopedTools`, and `resolveSkillDispatchTools`.

### Security Guarantee

Runtime tokens are filtered through every policy layer (profile, provider profile, global, agent, group, sender, sandbox, owner-only, subagent, inherited). A subagent policy that narrows the allowlist correctly strips broad tokens like `bundle-mcp` while preserving explicitly-allowed individual MCP/LSP selectors. The deny path works too: a parent that denies `bundle-mcp` prevents any MCP runtime from leaking to children.

## Evidence

### CI / Automated Tests

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tool-policy.test.ts src/gateway/tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts
```

All 121 tests passed (0 failures).

### New Tests Added (6 total)

| Test file | Tests | What they verify |
|-----------|:-----:|------------------|
| `tool-policy.test.ts` | 3 | Entry identification, policy-layer filtering, deny-layer removal of runtime selectors |
| `tool-resolution.exclude.test.ts` | 2 | Gateway path: token preservation AND narrow-policy filtering |
| `agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts` | 1 | Agent-tools path: token preservation in `createOpenClawCodingTools` |

### Real Behavior Proof

The fix was validated in the same scenario described in #85030:

1. Parent agent configured with `tools.allow` containing `bundle-mcp`, `probe__allowed` (MCP tool), and concrete tools
2. Subagent spawned via `sessions_spawn`
3. Child's `inheritedToolAllow` captured from session store
4. MCP runtime materialized for the child session
5. Child-visible MCP tools = intersection of inherited allowlist and materialized tools

Result: `probe__allowed` was present in the child's tool set; `probe__blocked` (not in the allowlist) was absent. The allowed MCP tool executed successfully via the production tool executor.

### Upstream Reference

Builds on the investigation and proof-of-concept from #92521 by @yu-xin-c.

target.title: fix(xai): bound stalled generated video download body reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gap where xAI generated-video downloads had no download-owned chunk-idle timeout on the success body reader. A mid-body stall only surfaced as a generic guarded-fetch `request timed out` (or waited the full request budget) instead of a clear download idle failure.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadXaiVideo`, pass a `chunkTimeoutMs` (half the resolved request budget) + `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`. The chunk-idle budget is shorter than the guarded-request deadline, so a mid-body stall produces the download-owned idle error before the generic request timeout. A continuously dripping CDN body resets the idle on every chunk and still hits the guarded request deadline.

`fetchWithSsrFGuard` already keeps its abort until `release()`, so a continuously dripping CDN body cannot hang forever on this path; the idle bound is the missing download-owned stall signal. Shared fetch/assert helpers are unchanged.

Non-overlapping: #108982 is a multi-provider video download batch and does not include xAI. #108796 is TTS WebSocket handshake tests only.

Collision check: no open hang-class PR on `downloadXaiVideo` / `extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.ts`.

## User Impact

Stalled xAI generated-video downloads fail with `xAI generated video download stalled after <timeout>ms` instead of only a generic request timeout. Continuously dripping bodies still die within the existing guarded request deadline.

## Evidence

Exact head: `c061e466764`
`oxfmt --check extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.ts extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.download.loopback.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/xai/video-generation-transport.download.loopback.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ rejects a stalled body with the download-owned idle timeout 1441ms
 ✓ rejects a continuously dripping CDN body within the guarded request deadline 335ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 412ms
 ✓ rejects a stalled body with the idle deadline before the guarded request deadline in an unmocked loopback 228ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Loopback proof

- **Stalled body (mocked guard)**: mock fetch, real `readResponseWithLimit` with `chunkTimeoutMs: 25` — rejects with `"xAI generated video download stalled after 25ms"` in 1441ms.
- **Drip body (unmocked)**: real `http.createServer` + real `fetch` + real `downloadXaiVideo` with `allowPrivateNetwork`, continuous 20ms drip — rejects via guarded request deadline.
- **Negative control**: idle-only `chunkTimeoutMs: 100` on a 20ms drip stays unsettled past 400ms.
- **Unmocked stall proof (new)**: real `http.createServer` sends initial bytes then stalls; `totalTimeoutMs: 300`, `idleTimeoutMs: 150` — idle error fires at ~150ms, well before the 300ms guard; `elapsedMs < totalTimeoutMs - 50` proves idle beat the guard.

### Not tested

Live xAI CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): keep spawn pipe streams UTF-8 safe across chunk splits
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Azure CLI login output captured from child_process spawn could show corrupted multibyte text (for example CJK or emoji) in terminal output and error messages when a UTF-8 code point was split across stdout/stderr chunk boundaries (`String(chunk)` per Buffer → U+FFFD).

Related prior art: #108518 (`provider-local-service` `setEncoding("utf8")`) and #109220 (`voice-call` ngrok tunnel logs).

## Why This Change Was Made

`azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions` pipes now decode stdout/stderr statefully with `setEncoding("utf8")` before line buffering and output forwarding.

## User Impact

Operators running Azure CLI login through the Microsoft Foundry extension see intact Unicode in terminal output and error-derived messages instead of `�` when output is chunked mid-character.

## Evidence

### Changes

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts` | +8/−4 — add `setEncoding("utf8")` before stdout/stderr data handlers |
| `extensions/microsoft-foundry/index.test.ts` | +73/−24 — mock regression test calling `azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions` + real-spawn integration test |
| `scripts/proof-setencoding-utf8.mjs` | +79/−0 — standalone proof script anyone can run to verify before/after behavior |

### Tests

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  95 passed (95)
```

### Proof

**1. Production-function regression test (mock spawn)**

Calls `azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions({})` through a controlled `spawn()` mock that returns a fake ChildProcess with `PassThrough` streams. Writes a 4-byte UTF-8 smiley (U+1F60A) split across two `stderr` writes at the exact byte boundary where raw `Buffer.toString()` would produce U+FFFD, then emits `close(1)`. Asserts the rejection error contains the cleanly reassembled `😊` — proving the production function's `setEncoding` + error-output path work correctly together.

**2. Real-spawn integration test**

Uses `vi.importActual` to bypass the module mock and get the real `spawn` from `node:child_process`. Spawns a real Node.js child (`process.execPath -e ...`) that writes `Buffer.from([0xf0, 0x9f, 0x98, 0x8a])` split across two `process.stdout.write` calls with a 10 ms delay — simulating real pipe chunking that Azure CLI would produce. Applies the same `setEncoding("utf8")` that the production fix uses, collects data chunks, and asserts the output is the clean `😊` without U+FFFD. This proves the stateful decoder mechanism works with real OS pipes and real child process I/O.

**3. Standalone proof script (`scripts/proof-setencoding-utf8.mjs`)**

Anyone can run `node scripts/proof-setencoding-utf8.mjs` to verify the before/after behavior on their own machine. Terminal output:

```
❌ WITHOUT setEncoding (old behaviour)
    per-chunk hex:              f09f  988a
    per-chunk String():          "�" + "��"
    joined result:              "���"
    has U+FFFD (�):              true

✅ WITH setEncoding (fix)
    per-chunk strings:           "😊"
    joined result:              "😊"
    has U+FFFD (�):              false
```

**4. Real spawned `az` end-to-end proof (see PR comment)**

Creates a fake `az` executable on an isolated PATH that writes a 4-byte UTF-8 smiley split across two `stderr` writes 50 ms apart, then spawns `az login --use-device-code` with and without `setEncoding("utf8")`. This exercises the exact same `spawn("az", ["login", "--use-device-code"], ...)` path as the production function, through a real OS pipe buffer. See the PR comment for live terminal output.

Combined proof coverage:

| Layer | What it proves | Method |
|-------|---------------|--------|
| Production function logic | `azLoginDeviceCodeWithOptions` handles setEncoding → data → accumulation → close → error correctly | Mock `spawn()` with `PassThrough` streams |
| Real OS pipe decoder | `setEncoding("utf8")` reassembles split bytes on real spawned pipes | Fake `az` on PATH, real `spawn()` with same args as production function |
| Reproducibility | Any operator can verify before/after on their machine | Standalone `scripts/proof-setencoding-utf8.mjs` |

### Non-goals / boundaries

- Does not add Azure CLI binary dependency to tests.
- Does not change `execAz` (uses `execFileSync` with `encoding: "utf-8"`) or `execAzAsync` (uses SDK `runExec` wrapper) — both already handle encoding correctly.

target.title: fix(tlon): bound Urbit auth response body drain to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The Urbit login flow in the Tlon extension reads the entire response body via `response.text()` solely to flush the stream so that `set-cookie` headers finalize. The body content is discarded. This call had no size bound — a misconfigured or hostile Urbit endpoint could stream gigabytes into process memory during login.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the unbounded `response.text()` body drain with a **streaming reader with a 64 KiB cumulative drain budget**. When the body stream is available (Node 18+, Bun, Deno), the reader reads chunks until the total drained bytes reach the threshold, then cancels the stream. The 64 KiB threshold is a **cumulative accounting cap** — a single producer chunk may push the total above 64 KiB because we check after each read, which avoids splitting chunks mid-stream. When no body stream is available (rare polyfill/edge case), the fallback `text()` path is preserved for compatibility.

The body content was always discarded; only the `set-cookie` header is consumed.

## User Impact

Urbit login no longer risks OOM from an oversized response body. Normal login flows (small JSON bodies) are completely unaffected. The cookie extraction behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/tlon/src/urbit/auth.ssrf.test.ts --run`: **5/5 passed** (2 existing SSRF + 3 new body drain tests).
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The three new tests cover: streamed body drain with cookie extraction, oversized stream cancellation after the 64 KiB cap, and the body-less fallback path.

### Real behavior proof (loopback drain)

Controlled loopback exercising the same drain pattern used in production:

```json
{"case":"under-cap","drained":1024,"cancelled":false,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=abc; Path=/; HttpOnly"}
{"case":"over-cap","drained":65536,"cancelled":true,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=xyz; Path=/; HttpOnly","note":"Stream cancelled after 64 KiB cumulative drain; cookie still available"}
{"case":"body-less-fallback","drained":-1,"cookie":"urbauth-~zod=fallback; Path=/; HttpOnly"}
```

- **Under-cap (1 KiB)**: drains fully, stream completes normally, cookie extracted.
- **Over-cap (256 KiB)**: drains exactly 65536 bytes (64 KiB), stream cancelled, cookie STILL extracted — the drain threshold prevents unbounded buffering without breaking auth.
- **Body-less fallback**: uses `text()` path, cookie extracted.

The 64 KiB threshold is intentionally a **cumulative read budget**, not a strict per-chunk allocation. Since `reader.read()` returns producer-defined chunks, a single chunk may push the total slightly above 64 KiB. This is safe: the threshold prevents unbounded accumulation, and the previous chunk (at most 64 KiB) is released before the next read.

target.title: refactor(channels): centralize inbound orchestration and remove internal compat
target.body:
Closes #109316

## What Problem This Solves

Internal and bundled message channels still assembled core-owned route, session, context, history, retry, dispatch, and delivery behavior through deprecated low-level compatibility surfaces. That duplicated lifecycle logic across transports and allowed public Plugin SDK compatibility APIs to become internal architecture.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core now owns normalized inbound turn planning and dispatch: route/envelope construction, direct-DM access, session conflict retry, history/media handling, session recording, durable delivery, feedback reflection, and lifecycle ordering. Bundled channels provide transport facts and native send/reaction/typing operations only. Internal callers use focused modern seams; shipped compatibility remains only at public SDK, released input/data, doctor/migration, or external dependency boundaries.

The stack is intentionally one PR but split into subsystem commits: core turn kernel, runtime compat removal, architecture guards, memory, Teams feedback, bundled channel migrations, direct-DM/envelope cleanup, tests, and generated SDK baseline.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Plugin authors keep shipped compatibility during its existing deprecation window. Maintainers get one core-owned inbound lifecycle, transport-thinner channels, and hard guards against new internal deprecated-facade use.

Non-test TypeScript using the task's `*.test.ts` exclusion: **+2522 / -2523, net -1 line**.

## Deprecation Triage

| Bucket | Final count | Decision |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| LEGITIMATE | 110 files / 308 raw marker lines | Retain only shipped SDK/public, released CLI/config/data, doctor/migration, or provider/dependency compatibility. Registry report: 258 deprecated records, 0 eligible for removal. |
| STALE INTERNAL | 0 remaining | All bundled/internal imports migrated to focused modern APIs. Guards fail on deprecated SDK facades and low-level channel runtime/access seams. |
| DEAD | 0 remaining | Caller and surface checks found no removable remaining marker-bearing declaration. Two dead lexical diagnostic compatibility probes were deleted; no removed-symbol tests were rewritten. |

Raw marker lines and compat registry records are different units: one declaration can be re-exported through multiple public barrels, while registry records track shipped removal windows.

<details>
<summary>LEGITIMATE keeps: every remaining non-test file outside plugin-sdk</summary>

| File | Keep rationale |
| --- | --- |

target.title: fix(feishu): lock timeoutMs preflight abort for stalled DNS lookup
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Feishu app registration goes through `fetchWithSsrFGuard`. Operators need a locked regression that a **stalled DNS/proxy preflight** is cancelled by the guard's existing top-level `timeoutMs` before any HTTP request is dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

ClawSweeper P1 on the prior tip: replacing `timeoutMs` with `AbortSignal.timeout()` does **not** add preflight protection — `fetchWithSsrFGuard` already converts `timeoutMs` into the preflight abort signal via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, and swapping owners only drops the shared `request timed out` diagnostic.

**This iteration (rebased on latest main + standalone L3 proof):**
- Rebuilt on latest `main` (`22563878857`)
- **Kept** guard `timeoutMs` (no production ownership change)
- Added stalled-lookup regression next to the existing hang-POST timeout proof, matching its outcome shape
- The registration API (`FeishuAppRegistrationFetchOptions`) is unchanged on current main — test typechecks and passes as-is
- **Added standalone non-mock proof** — runs production `fetchWithSsrFGuard` directly (no Vitest, no test injection)

## User Impact

- **Before:** No focused Feishu registration test that a never-resolving lookup aborts under `timeoutMs` without HTTP dispatch.
- **After:** That contract is locked; registration timeout semantics stay on the shared guard owner.

## Evidence

**Head SHA:** `6d7aab253ee`
**Base:** `22563878857`

### 🐚 Platinum: Standalone non-mock runtime proof (L3)

Runs `fetchWithSsrFGuard` directly with a never-resolving `lookupFn` and `timeoutMs: 80`:

```
$ node --import tsx /tmp/feishu-stall-proof.ts

[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 80ms (elapsed 84ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=https://accounts.feishu.cn/oauth/v1/app/registration
[feishu stall proof] version=standalone
[feishu stall proof] timed_out=true
[feishu stall proof] name=TimeoutError
[feishu stall proof] message=request timed out
[feishu stall proof] elapsed_ms=168
[feishu stall proof] host=LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
[feishu stall proof] date=2026-07-17T06:33:12.995Z
[feishu stall proof] result=PASS
```

**Key observations:**
- The first `[fetch-timeout]` line is the **production guard's own diagnostic** (not from test code) — proves `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` fires at 84ms
- `name=TimeoutError`, `message=request timed out` — shared diagnostic preserved
- `result=PASS` — all 4 assertions pass
- No HTTP dispatch happens (no fetchImpl was called)

### Regression test suite (11/11 pass)

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts --reporter verbose extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.10

 ✓ Feishu app registration > defaults unsafe begin polling lifetimes 183ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > clamps unsafe poll sleeps 13ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > prints scan-to-create QR codes 1ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > times out registration POSTs (TCP hang) 93ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > rejects with timeout when preflight lookup stalls 83ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > rejects Feishu API responses that exceed 16 MiB cap 178ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > parses under-cap JSON 19ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > sends bound reads through real SSRF guard 7ms
 ✓ Feishu app registration > wraps malformed JSON with feishu.api error 6ms
 ✓ feishu bound reads > rejects oversized response (OOM guard) 82ms
 ✓ feishu bound reads > parses well-formed JSON under cap 14ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
   Start at  13:33:36
   Duration  2.72s

Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Date: 2026-07-17T13:33:39+08:00
```

### Matched outcome shape (new test vs existing POST sibling)

| Assertion | Existing POST hang test | New stalled-DNS test |
|---|---|---|
| `lookupFn` | real DNS lookup → `127.0.0.1` | `stalledLookup` (never resolves) |
| abort mechanism | `timeoutMs` → preflight AbortSignal | `timeoutMs` → preflight AbortSignal |
| outcome | `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` | `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` |
| `fetchImpl` | reaches TCP listener | ❌ **not called** (never reaches HTTP) |
| elapsed window | ≥60ms, <2000ms | ≥60ms, <2000ms |

**Output breakdown:**

| Proof | Value | Assertion verified |
|---|---|---|
| Guard diagnostic | `fetch timeout after 80ms (elapsed 84ms)` | Guard's own log — production code path ✅ |
| `timed_out` | `true` | Request timed out ✅ |
| `name` | `TimeoutError` | Error type is TimeoutError ✅ |
| `message` | `request timed out` | Shared diagnostic preserved ✅ |
| `elapsed_ms` | `168` | ≥ 60 && < 2000 ✅ |
| `result` | `PASS` | All assertions pass ✅ |

### Test code

Located at `extensions/feishu/src/app-registration.test.ts:290-326` — placed as sibling of the existing "times out registration POSTs when accounts never return headers" test, using identical outcome shape (`timeoutMs: 80`, `then/catch` split, same elapsed window).

target.title: fix(auto-reply): deliverBindingPayload missing abortSignal check
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `deliverBindingPayload` does not check or propagate the dispatch abort signal, so plugin binding notifications could still be delivered via `routeReplyToOriginating`, `dispatcher.sendToolResult`, or `dispatcher.sendFinalReply` after the dispatch operation has been aborted.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deliverBindingPayload` was missing the same abort-signal guard that `sendPayloadAsync` (the sibling function) already implements:

1. **Check upfront**: `getDispatchAbortSignal()` + `.aborted` early return
2. **Propagate**: pass `abortSignal` to `routeReplyToOriginating` options
3. **Re-check**: after the async `routeReplyToOriginating` call, check `.aborted` again before falling through to `sendToolResult`/`sendFinalReply`

Since all callers of `deliverBindingPayload` are in the same closure that already has `getDispatchAbortSignal()` — no parameter changes needed.

## User Impact

Users of plugin bindings may see fewer stale/misdirected binding notifications when a dispatch operation is aborted (e.g. session timeout, manual cancellation). No behavior change for normal (non-aborted) dispatch paths.

## Evidence

- **Real environment tested**: Linux x64, Node 22, branch `fix/bug-020-deliver-binding-payload-abort-signal`
- **Exact test command run after this patch**:

  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/dispatch-from-config.test.ts
  ```

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Streaming pre-read bound (primary path):** When the response body stream is available, the function now uses `readResponseWithLimit` to enforce the 4 MiB cap **before** buffering — the stream is read in chunks and cancelled on overflow, matching the existing `materializeGuardedResponse` pattern used by `fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`.

**Post-hoc fallback (body-less path):** When the body stream is unavailable (rare polyfill or mock edge case), the function falls back to `text()` with a byte-length check after buffering. This preserves backward compatibility with `DiscordGatewayFetch` implementations that return body-less mock responses.

**Non-transient overflow:** Size overflow now throws as non-transient (`transient: false`) so the detail message propagates to callers instead of being swallowed by the generic "fetch failed" wrapper.

## User Impact

Discord Gateway connections now reject oversized/hostile metadata responses **before** buffering the full body into memory. Normal responses (a few KB of JSON) are completely unaffected. The `DiscordGatewayFetch` type contract is backward-compatible — callers that don't provide `body` continue to work via the post-hoc fallback.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.test.ts --run`: **8/8 passed**.
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed.
- The test coverage includes: body-less success, body-less oversized rejection, **real loopback HTTP streaming oversized rejection** (pre-read bound verified), and a load-bearing mutation test.

### Real behavior proof (loopback HTTP streaming path)

The new test creates a real HTTP server streaming chunked JSON and verifies the streaming reader rejects at the 4 MiB boundary:

```
✓ returns parsed gateway info when response body is within the 4 MiB cap
✓ rejects oversized response via loopback HTTP (streaming pre-read bound)
✓ rejects oversized body-less response via post-hoc fallback guard
✓ mutation: removing both guards causes over-cap bodies to be accepted silently
```

The streaming rejection path uses `readResponseWithLimit` which reads chunks in a bounded loop via `reader.read()` and cancels the stream on overflow — the same pattern already used by `materializeGuardedResponse` in the guarded fetch path.

`@slack/web-api` defaults `timeout` to `0` (no deadline). One-shot Slack WebClient and write clients could hang forever when Slack stalled. Lookup already defaulted to 30s; web/write did not.

target.title: fix(browser): honor abortSignal during Playwright click-and-hold delay
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`clickViaPlaywright`'s click-and-hold delay in `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` slept with a bare `setTimeout(resolve, delayMs)`, where `delayMs` can be up to `ACT_MAX_CLICK_DELAY_MS = 5_000` (`act-policy.ts:22`). The interaction `AbortSignal` is already in scope and is checked via `throwIfInteractionAborted(signal)` right before and after the sleep — but the sleep itself was not abortable.

When the signal fires mid-hold, the caller-visible promise does reject promptly (the `abortPromise` race in `awaitActionWithAbort`, `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts:488`), but the *action chain* is orphaned: the ref'd 5 s timer keeps sleeping after the caller is gone, then throws at the post-delay check. While orphaned it pins the event loop for the remainder of the hold, and it delays the navigation-guard teardown that only runs after the action settles — the delayed-navigation observation plus the 250 ms grace and the final `assertPageNavigationCompletedSafely` (`pw-tools-core.interactions.ts:569-590`), and with an SSRF policy active the `page.route("**")` interception installed by `withPageNavigationRequestGuard` (`pw-session.ts:1663`) stays attached to the tab for the rest of the hold as well.

## Why This Change Was Made

The hold is now `await sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` (`packages/retry/src/index.ts:21`, re-exported via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/runtime-env`, already imported elsewhere in this plugin, e.g. `sleep` in `cdp.helpers.ts`). `sleepWithAbort` clears its timer and rejects on abort, so the orphaned chain unwinds at the abort event instead of after the full remaining delay. The pre/post `throwIfInteractionAborted(signal)` checks are unchanged, so behavior with no signal or no abort is identical.

The surfaced error is unchanged: `clickViaPlaywright` registers its abort listener (which rejects the race with `signal.reason`) before the action starts, so the race still rejects with the original abort reason — the proof below shows byte-identical rejection messages before and after. No new config, no new env, no SDK surface change.

Pattern reference: #108561 (merged) did the same `setTimeout` → `sleepWithAbort` swap for the Discord gateway READY backoff. Sibling #109617 covers the browser tab-discovery poll; this PR covers the click-and-hold hold delay — disjoint code paths.

## User Impact

- Cancelling an agent browser click with a hold delay (e.g. a 5 s click-and-hold) no longer leaves an orphaned action chain sleeping in the background: the timer is cleared at the abort event and the event loop can drain ~immediately (proof: 5010 ms → 338 ms).
- The post-interaction navigation guard (delayed-navigation observation, grace window, final safety recheck, and request interception when an SSRF policy is configured) is released at the abort instead of up to 5 s later, so follow-up interactions on the same tab no longer run under a stale, aborted interaction's guard state.
- Happy path is untouched: without an abort the click still waits the full `delayMs` before dispatching (locked by regression test).

## Evidence

### Signal path — full chain (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool opts | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 708 | `const signal = opts.signal` |
| Abort race | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 713-740 | `abortPromise` rejects with `signal.reason`; listener registered before the action runs |
| Hold delay (this PR) | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 758 | `await sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` — timer cleared + rejection on abort |
| Sleep impl | `packages/retry/src/index.ts` | 21 | `sleepWithAbort`: `clearTimeout` + `reject(new Error("aborted", { cause: signal.reason }))` on the abort event |
| Race | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 488-506 | `Promise.race([actionPromise, abortPromise])`; late action rejection swallowed to avoid unhandled rejections |
| Guard teardown | `pw-tools-core.interactions.ts` | 569-590 | grace + `assertPageNavigationCompletedSafely` run in `finally` once the action settles — now reached at abort time |

### Real behavior proof — production `clickViaPlaywright`, real `AbortController`, wall-clock

Uncommitted proof script drives the production `clickViaPlaywright` (`resolvedPage` stub whose `locator()` returns an observed locator, `selector` + `delayMs: 5000`, no CDP connection), aborts 100 ms into the 5 000 ms hold, then measures `process.getActiveResourcesInfo()` Timeout entries and the `beforeExit` timestamp (when the event loop could actually drain). No mocks, no vitest.

**Before fix (main @ 9638c3ae07)**

```json
{
  "delayMs": 5000,
  "abortAtMs": 100,
  "events": [["hover", 2], ["abort()", 106], ["settled", 149]],
  "callerRejected": true,
  "rejectionMessage": "proof: user cancelled click-and-hold",
  "rejectElapsedMs": 149,
  "hoverFired": true,
  "clickFired": false,
  "timeoutResourcesAfterReject": 1,
  "eventLoopDrainedAtMs": 5010,
  "verdict": "BUG: caller rejected but the orphaned hold-delay timer pins the event loop for the full 5000ms"
}
```

**After fix (this PR)**

```json
{
  "delayMs": 5000,
  "abortAtMs": 100,
  "events": [["hover", 4], ["abort()", 106], ["settled", 138]],
  "callerRejected": true,
  "rejectionMessage": "proof: user cancelled click-and-hold",
  "rejectElapsedMs": 138,
  "hoverFired": true,
  "clickFired": false,
```

The new regression test fails on the unpatched code and passes on this branch:

| Version | `unwinds the hold-delay action chain promptly when aborted mid-delay` | `still waits the full hold delay before clicking when not aborted` |
|---|---|---|
| main @ 9638c3ae07 | **fails** — post-abort navigation recheck still pending 1 000 ms after the abort (orphan sleeps the full 5 000 ms first) | passes |
| this PR | **passes** — recheck completes within the 250 ms observation + 250 ms grace after the abort | passes |

Revert is exactly the production hunk above (`sleepWithAbort(delayMs, signal)` → bare `setTimeout(resolve, delayMs)`); no test edits between runs.

### Regression test

`extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.interactions.click-delay.abort.test.ts` (colocated, uses the shared `pw-tools-core.test-harness.ts` mocks): aborts a real `AbortController` 100 ms into a 5 000 ms hold and asserts (a) rejection with the original abort reason, (b) `locator.click` never fires, (c) the existing force-disconnect-on-abort call still happens with `reason: "click aborted"`, and (d) the orphaned chain's navigation recheck settles promptly instead of after the full hold. Second test locks the happy path: without abort, the click fires only after the full 5 000 ms.

target.title: fix: gateway.cmd launcher garbles non-ASCII profile paths on non-CJK Windows locales
target.body:
Closes #108774

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Windows users whose profile path contains non-ASCII characters outside the CJK range (Turkish, Cyrillic, Greek, Western European accents, ...) can install OpenClaw but the managed Gateway never starts: the generated `gateway.cmd` launcher garbles the profile path and the launch chain dies with "The system cannot find the path specified" / `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

#107751 fixed this failure for CJK locales by encoding the launcher in the system ANSI code page — but only on locales where ANSI == OEM, and it deliberately left windows-125x hosts on plain UTF-8 ("ANSI bytes would just be a different flavor of wrong there"). On those hosts (e.g. Turkish: ANSI 1254, OEM 857) cmd.exe still reads the UTF-8 launcher in its OEM code page and the mojibake from #108774 persists.

## Why This Change Was Made

cmd.exe parses batch files with the **console code page**, which a fresh console (Task Scheduler, Startup folder, double-click) initializes from the boot-time registry `OEMCP` — not from the ANSI page, and not from whatever a parent session last `chcp`'d to. So the launcher encoder now targets the OEM page directly instead of approximating it via ANSI:

- `resolveWindowsOemEncoding()` (new, `src/infra/windows-encoding.ts`) reads `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Nls\CodePage\OEMCP` once (cached) through a narrow `queryWindowsRegistryValue` export that reuses the existing reg.exe query logic in `src/infra/windows-install-roots.ts`.
- `encodeWindowsLauncherScript` (`src/infra/windows-launcher-encoding.ts`) encodes non-ASCII `.cmd` content to that OEM page with the same `@rem openclaw-launcher-encoding=<label>` marker and fail-closed round-trip verification introduced in #107751. The `CMD_ANSI_EQUALS_OEM_ENCODINGS` special case is deleted: on CJK locales OEMCP == ACP, so those hosts resolve the identical labels (gbk/big5/shift_jis/euc-kr/windows-874) and produce byte-identical launchers — no behavior change there.
- Newly covered OEM single-byte pages: 437, 720, 737, 775, 850, 852, 855, 857, 858, 860–863, 865, 866, 869 (iconv-lite `cp###` labels; iconv-lite 0.7.2 is already a root dependency since #107751).
- The decoder is untouched — the marker mechanism was already label-generic, so launchers written by any prior version still read back correctly (including legacy `gb18030`-marked files).

Design notes:

- **Why not `%APPDATA%`/`%ProgramFiles%` substitution (the issue's suggested fix):** the ClawSweeper review on #108774 correctly notes that would break custom npm prefixes, portable Node, and version managers. This fix keeps the installer-resolved paths and makes the encoding correct instead.
- **Round-trip verification decoder:** WHATWG `TextDecoder` where its tables match Windows (gbk/big5/shift_jis/windows-874 — it also flags best-fit hazards like shift_jis `¥` → 0x5C); iconv's own decode for euc-kr (Node ICU is KS X 1001-only and false-rejects cp949/UHC extension syllables) and for all `cp###` pages (no WHATWG decoder exists; WHATWG `ibm866` even disagrees with Windows CP866 at 0x1A/0x1C/0x7F). Safe because iconv-lite never best-fits — unmappable characters become `?` and fail the round-trip, aborting the install with the existing clear error.
- **Deliberate omissions, commented in the map:** CP864 (Arabic OEM) repurposes ASCII `0x25 "%"`, which generated cmd scripts contain, and the corruption would round-trip cleanly through iconv's own model — modern Arabic Windows uses OEM 720 (included) anyway. CP1258 (Vietnamese, the one locale whose OEMCP is a windows-125x page) is omitted because iconv-lite cannot round-trip Vietnamese combining forms; it keeps today's UTF-8 fallback instead of turning mojibake into a hard install error. Hosts with the "UTF-8 worldwide" beta (OEMCP 65001) keep plain UTF-8, which is correct there.

## User Impact

`openclaw gateway install` + `gateway start` now works for Windows accounts with Turkish/Cyrillic/Greek/Western-European/etc. non-ASCII usernames — previously the P0 release-blocker path in #108774. CJK users see byte-identical output to #107751. ASCII-only installs are untouched (encoder still short-circuits before any code-page probe).

## Evidence

**Live before/after on a real affected host** — Windows 11 Pro, Turkish locale (registry ACP 1254 / OEMCP 857), i.e. exactly the ANSI≠OEM case #107751 left open. A launcher with `buildTaskScript`-shaped content (`cd /d`, `set "OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=..."`, node invocation) pointing into a `...\ev-yiğit-öğün\` profile directory, executed under a CP857 console (what Task Scheduler provides):

Before (bytes exactly as origin/main writes them on this host — UTF-8 fallback):

```
Sistem belirtilen yolu bulamıyor.            <- cd /d failed ("The system cannot find the path specified")
Error: Cannot find module 'C:\...\ev-yi─şit-├Â─ş├╝n\probe.js'   <- UTF-8 bytes misread as CP857
exit code: 1
```

After (bytes from the fixed `encodeWindowsLauncherScript()`, real production function + real registry read, which resolved `cp857` and emitted the `@rem openclaw-launcher-encoding=cp857` marker):

```
PROBE_OK cwd=C:\...\scratchpad\ev-yiğit-öğün
PROBE_OK stateDir=C:\...\scratchpad\ev-yiğit-öğün\state
exit code: 0
```

**Tests** (all pass, `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ...`): `src/infra/windows-launcher-encoding.test.ts`, `src/infra/windows-encoding.test.ts`, `src/daemon/schtasks.test.ts`, `src/daemon/schtasks.install.test.ts`, `src/infra/windows-task-restart.test.ts` — 49 tests. New regression cases: cp857 Turkish path round-trip with marker, cp850 Western European, OEMCP-65001 stays UTF-8, unrepresentable characters on a single-byte OEM page fail the install fail-closed. All #107751 CJK cases (GBK/UTF-8 byte-collision, cp949 UHC syllables, 🚀 rejection) pass unchanged with OEM-based resolution.

`oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean on all touched files; `tsgo -p tsconfig.core.json` reports no errors in touched files (the 42 pre-existing errors on this machine reproduce identically on a clean `origin/main` checkout — local env, unrelated).

target.title: refactor(transcripts): add SQLite storage backend to TranscriptsStore
target.body:
## Summary

Add meeting-capture transcript tables to the shared state DB and add an optional SQLite storage backend to TranscriptsStore.

- Problem: Transcript session metadata and utterances are stored as loose JSON files on disk, with no transaction safety or concurrent-access guarantees.
- Solution: Add `transcript_sessions` and `transcript_utterances` tables to the shared state schema (STRICT, CHECK, FOREIGN KEY). TranscriptsStore now accepts an optional `OpenClawStateDatabase` handle; when provided, all writes go through `runOpenClawStateWriteTransaction`. File-based backend is preserved for backward compatibility.
- What changed: `src/state/openclaw-state-schema.sql` (+48 lines), `src/state/openclaw-state-schema.generated.ts` (regenerated DDL), `src/state/openclaw-state-db.generated.d.ts` (+36 lines, Kysely types), `src/state/openclaw-state-db.ts` (schema version 3→4), `src/transcripts/store.ts` (+299/-10 lines, dual backend)
- What did NOT change: Summary artifacts remain filesystem-only; `TranscriptSessionDescriptor` / `TranscriptUtterance` types unchanged; public API of TranscriptsStore unchanged (optional constructor param).

## Change Type

- [x] Refactor required for the fix

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration

## Linked Issue

- Related #98986
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Meeting-capture transcripts (real-time voice/caption recordings from Discord, Google Meet, etc.) are currently stored as individual JSON files per session with append-only JSONL for utterances. This lacks transaction safety, makes concurrent access unsafe, and prevents integration with the shared state DB that other subsystems (push-web, APNs, cron) already use.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: TranscriptsStore reads/writes through SQLite when a state DB handle is provided
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 24.13, branch `refactor/transcripts-sqlite-98986`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/transcripts/store.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  6 passed (6)
```

- Observed result after fix: All 6 existing transcript store tests pass with the file-backed path unchanged.
- What was not tested: Live meeting-capture transcription flow with SQLite backend; SQLite-specific test coverage for the new tables.

## Root Cause

N/A — this is an incremental migration to shared SQLite storage following the established pattern from push-web (#103294) and APNs (#108543).

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. The store API is unchanged; callers opt into SQLite by passing a state DB handle.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: All 6 existing file-backed store tests pass; schema DDL verified against upstream/main
- Edge cases checked: Missing state DB handle (falls back to file backend); qualified session ID selectors (date-prefixed queries)
- What you did NOT verify: Live transcription flow; SQLite-specific test coverage

target.title: fix(cli-runner): restore history for SQLite-backed CLI resumes
target.body:
Related: #98236

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users resuming CLI-backed sessions would lose prior OpenClaw history after transcripts became SQLite-backed. Normal CLI, gateway, and cron paths persist a `sqlite:` transcript marker, but the CLI history loader still treated that marker as a filesystem path and reported that no transcript existed.

The same symptom could recur after moving a supported state-directory backup to a different absolute path because persisted markers retain the old path even though the restored per-agent database is now authoritative at the new location.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI runner now recognizes SQLite transcript markers, validates their session and agent identity, and reads from the current canonical store through the storage-neutral session accessor. The same canonical session target is passed through context-engine bootstrap, post-turn, and maintenance rewrites, so stale marker metadata cannot redirect reads or writes after a state-directory relocation.

The accessor streams only the newest complete rows within the existing 5 MiB JSONL-compatible window, restores the session envelope when the tail is truncated, and preserves migration, branch-safety, active-leaf selection, and message-cap behavior. Transcript existence uses a `LIMIT 1` lookup instead of synchronously aggregating every row on each CLI turn.

For retry and fallback paths where the current user turn was already persisted, history readers exclude that exact idempotency key after active-branch selection. This keeps the current turn out of lifecycle history, context-engine pre-prompt snapshots, and reseed `<conversation_history>` while preserving the same message once in `<next_user_message>`.

The previous short-header-read proposal and regression were intentionally removed as part of this PR redirect; this PR is now scoped to SQLite-backed CLI history restoration.

This is distinct from #108851, which bounds gateway message pagination through a derived active-message projection; it does not repair the CLI runner's marker existence or raw-history path. This change adds no schema, migration, configuration, default, or external public API surface.

## User Impact

CLI resumes, lifecycle hooks, context-engine synchronization, and allowed reseed flows can again use the active OpenClaw history stored in SQLite, including after a supported state-directory relocation. Retry and fallback turns no longer replay the current user message as prior history. Oversized transcripts remain bounded to the newest safe 5 MiB tail instead of loading the complete transcript.

## Evidence

- Initial RED on the test-first commit: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29512957643), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29512957643/job/87670775318) — 27 passed, 2 failed; marker existence returned `false` and oversized SQLite history returned `[]`.
- Review-gap RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29520108279), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29520108279/job/87694811630) — 31 passed, 2 failed; the relocated marker was rejected and existence still invoked full transcript stats.
- Memory-bound RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29522181652), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29522181652/job/87701667581) — tail selection still requested `event_json`, so an over-budget row was materialized before the JavaScript byte check.
- Context-target RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29524447512), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29524447512/job/87709238990) — the runtime transcript target still resolved a relocated session to the stale marker path.
- Live baseline RED through the real `pnpm openclaw agent --local` entry point with an isolated test-only CLI backend: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29549165465), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29549165465/job/87787840045) — the second turn saw zero prior messages and the provider gate blocked execution.
- Maintenance-target RED: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29553169268), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29553169268/job/87799830946) — the rewrite scope still included `storePath`, and file-backed maintenance was incorrectly converted to a SQLite marker.
- Persisted retry-turn RED on test-first commit `e141bfb6a441c48884f0d3698cce480f6bf4894e`, using the repository runner on Node 24.15.0 — 3 focused files failed as expected (3 failed, 94 passed): the current text appeared twice in the reseed prompt, hook/context-engine reads lacked the exclusion key, and SQLite history still contained the current turn.
- Final GREEN on exact fix head `d7a04d16f19baf2172ba45c654b2636497cf95a4`, pinned to base `44b01a1e5ab69357e46b0ec945b080290ef13873`: [run](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29557720712), [job](https://github.com/mushuiyu886/openclaw/actions/runs/29557720712/job/87813405498) — 10 focused files and 274 tests passed, including persisted retry-turn deduplication and a real two-database SQLite relocation rewrite control.
- The same exact-head job passed targeted `oxfmt`/`oxlint`, dependency-export deadcode checks, core `tsgo`, and patch whitespace validation.
- The same exact-head live proof ran two turns through `pnpm openclaw agent --local`: `sqlite_marker=true`, `second_hook_history_count=2`, both first-turn messages were present, the test-only CLI provider was invoked twice, and the second turn returned `provider-called`.
- Final `codex review --base origin/main` found no confirmed new defect; its Node 24.15.0 verification also passed 7 files / 168 tests and 3 adjacent files / 146 tests.

Verification covers the OpenClaw SQLite transcript-to-CLI-history production path on GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 24, isolated state/config/workspace data, and a test-only CLI backend. It does not exercise a real third-party provider, browser, or cross-platform runtime.

target.title: fix(ai): bound openai-chatgpt-responses WebSocket with handshakeTimeout and maxPayload
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `connectWebSocket` function in `openai-chatgpt-responses` creates a WebSocket connection without any handshake timeout or message size limit. If the server accepts TCP but never completes the WebSocket upgrade, the connection hangs indefinitely. Oversized messages could also cause OOM.

**Solution**: Implement transport-neutral bounds using the existing lifecycle cleanup path rather than `ws`-specific constructor options:
- **Handshake timeout**: `setTimeout`-based 30s deadline that calls `socket.close()` and rejects the promise. Unlike `ws`-specific `handshakeTimeout`, this works across Node, Bun, and browser globals.
- **Message size limit**: Per-frame byte check in `parseWebSocket` rejecting oversized messages with WebSocket close code 1009. Unlike `ws`-specific `maxPayload`, this is enforced at the message decoding layer regardless of runtime.
- **Regression tests**: Stalled-handshake timeout and oversized-message rejection tests using `vi.useFakeTimers` and mock WebSockets.

**What changed**: Two files:
- `packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts` — Added `CONNECT_WS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS` (30s), `MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES` (16MB), handshake timer in `connectWebSocket()`, message size check in `parseWebSocket()`, test exports.
- Test file — Handshake timeout and oversized message regression coverage.

**What did NOT change**: No API changes, no `ws`-specific options on the constructor, no changes to `getWebSocketConstructor()`, `acquireWebSocket()`, or the SSE fallback path. No `docs/.local/` artifacts.

Fixes #109566

---

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #109566
- **In scope**: Transport-neutral handshake timeout + message size limit + regression tests
- **Out of scope**: WS-specific constructor options, SSE fallback, browser WebSocket globals

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Unbounded WebSocket handshake wait and oversized message OOM risk in openai-chatgpt-responses provider

**Real environment tested**: Test-only (transport-neutral bounds verified via `vi.useFakeTimers` and mock WebSocket classes)

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
git diff packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```diff
+const CONNECT_WS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000;
+const MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
+
+const handshakeTimer = setTimeout(() => {
+  if (settled) return;
+  settled = true;
+  cleanup();
+  socket.close(WEBSOCKET_MESSAGE_TOO_BIG_CLOSE_CODE, "handshake timeout");
+  reject(new Error("WebSocket connection handshake timed out"));
+}, connectTimeoutMs ?? CONNECT_WS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS);
+handshakeTimer.unref?.();
+
+// In cleanup():
+clearTimeout(handshakeTimer);
+
+// In parseWebSocket onMessage:
+if (text.length > MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES) {
+  socket.close(WEBSOCKET_MESSAGE_TOO_BIG_CLOSE_CODE, "message exceeds size limit");
+  failed = new CodexProtocolError(...);
+  done = true;
+  wake();
+  return;
+}
```

**Observed result after the fix**: Both bounds are transport-neutral, working across Node, Bun, and browser globals. Handshake timeout uses `setTimeout` + `clearTimeout` — a standard JS pattern. Message size is checked at decode time, not at the WebSocket constructor level.

**What was not tested**: No real OpenAI API call. No real stalled-handshake scenario against OpenAI infrastructure.

---

## Tests and validation

```bash
pnpm test -- packages/ai/src/providers/openai-chatgpt-responses.test.ts
```

Two new tests:
1. `"rejects a stalled WebSocket upgrade with a handshake timeout error"` — verifies `connectWebSocket` rejects after timeout when socket never opens/errors/closes
2. `"rejects oversized WebSocket messages exceeding MAX_WS_MESSAGE_BYTES"` — verifies `parseWebSocket` error on 17MB message

---

## Risk checklist

- [x] Backwards compatible — no API changes
- [x] Transport-neutral — works on Node, Bun, browser globals
- [x] Follows `clearTimeout`/`setTimeout` pattern used elsewhere in codebase (xai/tts.ts, realtime-voice-bridge.ts)
- [x] merge-risk: low — ~50 lines net, focused scope, regression tests added

target.title: fix(browser): keep tab reachability retry delay abortable
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where cancelling a browser tab operation during the reachability retry delay would wait the full delay before responding to the cancellation.

`ensureBrowserRunning` used `new Promise(setTimeout)` for the 250ms retry delay between reachability probes. When the request `AbortSignal` fired during this delay, the function waited the entire `TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS` before calling `signal.throwIfAborted()`, adding unnecessary latency to cancellation-sensitive callers.

## Why This Change Was Made

The retry delay now uses `sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal)` which rejects immediately when the signal fires, so the caller is notified of the cancellation during the delay rather than after it.

Related prior art: #108561 (discord gateway READY retry abortSignal), #108408 (feishu retry abortSignal propagation).

## User Impact

Browser tab operations (close, focus, select) cancelled during the 250ms reachability retry window respond to user cancellation up to 250ms faster.

## Evidence

### Scope

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Head | `eac9fd9a2f5` |
| Files | `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts` (+4/−5) · `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` (+1/−1) |
| Net | +5 / −6 across 2 files |

### Production change (behavior)

```ts
// Before
await new Promise((resolve) => { setTimeout(resolve, RETRY_DELAY_MS); });
signal?.throwIfAborted();

// After
await sleepWithAbort(TAB_REACHABILITY_RETRY_DELAY_MS, signal);
```

### Real-timer timing proof

A standalone Node.js script (`scripts/proof-109536-abort-timing.mjs`) compares the two patterns with real `performance.now()` timers and a real `AbortController`. Each scenario is run 5 times with the abort signal firing 50ms into the 250ms retry delay:

```
--- BEFORE (old code) ---
  Run 1: 250.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 2: 250.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 3: 250.3 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 4: 251.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)
  Run 5: 250.2 ms  ✗ ABORTED (This operation was aborted)

--- AFTER (new code: sleepWithAbort) ---
  Run 1: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 2: 50.6 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 3: 50.5 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 4: 51.0 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
  Run 5: 50.8 ms  ✗ ABORTED (aborted)
```

- **BEFORE**: consistently ~250ms — always waits the full retry delay before noticing the abort.
- **AFTER**: consistently ~50ms — rejects as soon as the abort signal fires, eliminating up to 200ms of unnecessary wait.

The same abort-propagation invariant is additionally covered by the fake-timer unit test at `tabs.test.ts:345`.

### Local gates (touched surface)

| Gate | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unit | `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts` | **22 passed** / 1 file |

### Proof

The existing test "does not retry or mutate after cancellation during the retry delay" covers this scenario: it advances past the first reachability check, aborts the signal, then verifies no reachability retry occurred. With `sleepWithAbort`, the abort is detected immediately during the delay rather than after it expires, and the error message changes from `"cancelled"` (from `throwIfAborted`) to `"aborted"` (from `sleepWithAbort`).

Real-timer proof confirms the timing improvement holds with real wall-clock timers, not only with fake timers.

---

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(music): stop hanging when generated asset downloads drip forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where music generation providers (e.g. fal) could hang forever when a CDN dripped the audio body slowly enough to reset per-chunk idle timers. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body.

Additionally:
1. Restores transient HTTP retry that was lost when the non-2xx validation was placed outside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`.
2. Skips diagnostic body reads for retryable 5xx statuses so a dripping error body does not consume the shared wall-clock deadline before the retry attempt starts.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three changes in `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset`:

1. **Wall-clock deadline**: One deadline spans headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` → `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`.

2. **Retry inside the wrapper**: Bounded non-2xx status validation now runs inside `executeProviderOperationWithRetry`'s operation callback. When the CDN returns HTTP 503, the error is thrown inside the retry loop so `isTransientProviderOperationError` can retry it.

3. **Skip body reads for 5xx**: Retryable statuses (500/502/503/504) cancel the response body immediately instead of reading it for diagnostics. A dripping 5xx body could otherwise consume the full wall-clock deadline, leaving the retry attempt with effectively no remaining budget.

Non-overlapping: #108982 bounds video-generation downloads; #109076 bounds Discord webhook bodies.

## User Impact

- Generated music downloads fail within the configured timeout when a CDN body trickles forever.
- Transient CDN errors (503, etc.) with dripping bodies are retried immediately — the body is cancelled so the retry gets a full budget.
- Non-retryable errors (400, etc.) still include bounded diagnostic detail.
- Music generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

## Evidence

Exact head: `dee8f741c1da3899930e3602cf858d0e6072632d`

`oxfmt --check src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ bounds a dripping download body with one wall-clock deadline 284ms
 ✓ throws on non-2xx HTTP status without retry 18ms
 ✓ retries on transient HTTP status before succeeding 268ms
 ✓ skips diagnostic body read on retryable status so deadline survives for retry 264ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 410ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  5 passed (5)
```

- **Drip body (200)**: continuous drip with timeoutMs=250 → rejects with wall-clock timeout.
- **Non-2xx (400)**: immediate 400 → throws HTTP status error without retry (400 is explicitly non-retryable), includes diagnostic body detail.
- **Retry (immediate 503 → 200)**: first request returns 503 with immediate body → retried → second request succeeds. Proves `requestCount === 2`.
- **Retry (dripping 503 → 200)**: first request returns 503 with continuous 15ms drip → body cancelled immediately (not read) → retry completes within 264ms. Proves the deadline survives for the retry attempt when the error body is skipped.
- **Negative control**: idle-only chunkTimeoutMs on a drip → stays unsettled past 400ms. Proves old code path has no wall-clock bound.

### Mutation check

Without fix (stash provider-assets.ts): `retries on transient` FAIL — 503 not retried.
With fix restored: `retries on transient` PASS — `requestCount === 2`.

### Not tested

Live fal CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

The hints were passive native-title spans, so their content was not reliably available to click, touch, or keyboard users. ## Why This Change Was Made The overview hints are now focusable buttons backed by Web Awesome tooltips with stable target IDs. Clicking the same hint again closes it, and Escape dismissal allows the next activation to reopen it normally. ## Evidence - Before: clicking a `?` left the Usage Overview unchanged and rendered no explanatory content. - After: clicking the Messages hint renders the localized tooltip above the control; a second click closes it. - Unit: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/usage/view-overview.test.ts` — 13 tests passed, including all nine button/tooltip associations and the declarative multi-trigger contract. - Real Chromium E2E: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.ui-e2e.config.ts --configLoader runner ui/src/e2e/usage-cost-analysis.e2e.test.ts` — 1 test passed, covering hover, focus/blur, click open/close, keyboard activation, and Escape dismissal. - Static checks: targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, Control UI i18n verification, UI `tsgo`, and `git diff --check` passed. - Rebase proof: the branch was rebased without conflict onto the live `upstream/main` used by GitHub's current PR merge result; the post-rebase unit and Chromium E2E checks passed again. - Fresh autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; patch correct (0.96 confidence). ### Before Clicking the Messages `?` leaves the overview unchanged; no hint content is rendered. ### After Clicking the same hint renders its localized tooltip above the control.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

target.title: fix(qa-lab): preserve emoji in Matrix timeout diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix QA tool-progress timeout diagnostics shorten observed event bodies to a 240-code-unit preview. When an emoji began at the existing raw `slice(0, 237)` boundary, the later JSON diagnostic serialized only its high surrogate as an escaped `\\ud83d`, discarding the complete character and making the timeout evidence misleading.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared `truncateUtf16Safe` helper now backs off to a complete Unicode code-point boundary while retaining the existing preview budget and suffix. Both preview-wait and final-wait diagnostics use the same formatter.

## User Impact

Matrix QA timeout failures no longer expose a half-character escape when observed messages cross the Unicode truncation boundary, so the retained failure evidence stays well-formed and actionable.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qa-lab/src/live-transports/matrix/scenarios/scenario-runtime-tool-progress-diagnostics.test.ts` (2 tests passed on Node 24.15.0)
- Added exact-boundary regression coverage for both exported timeout builders.
- Targeted `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Pre-commit autoreview: clean, no actionable findings (0.85 confidence).
- Exact-head `build-artifacts`, type checks, lint, and aggregate CI gate passed.
- Verified the focused SDK boundary at exact head: both package export maps, the SDK entrypoint registry, and SDK docs include `text-utility-runtime`; four sibling Matrix QA modules use the same subpath.
- Downloaded the exact-head `dist-runtime-build` artifact and loaded `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` through its packaged Node shim. `truncateUtf16Safe` resolved as a function, and the boundary probe produced no half-surrogate escape or UTF-8 replacement.
- [Real Matrix timeout proof](https://github.com/Leon-SK668/openclaw/actions/runs/29559974223) passed against exact PR head `2fd3a9d3d9f9e3e85a347fa84dc1c689c8cef776` on Node 24.15.0 with disposable Tuwunel v1.5.1. The production QA scenario registered real Matrix clients, created/joined a room, sent the trigger plus `m.replace` progress events, then exercised the actual 15-second final-event timeout path.
- The uploaded `matrix-timeout-proof-2fd3a9d3d9f9e3e85a347fa84dc1c689c8cef776` artifact (`sha256:04d488fbaf4265ed3c875e03572c469dedc58f469a95379ed60e044dc1d505f9`) contains the redacted timeout log and route inventory. Assertions confirm a preserved boundary emoji, retreat before a split surrogate pair, no escaped half surrogate, no lone surrogate, no replacement character, and a valid UTF-8 round trip.

target.title: fix(openai): prevent device-code login hangs on stalled requests
target.body:
Related: #104477

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenAI device-code login could remain stuck indefinitely when an `auth.openai.com` request stopped responding before headers arrived or while its response body was being read.

The existing 15-minute authorization deadline only bounded the polling loop. A single user-code, poll, or token-exchange request could outlive that deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three device-code operations now use the canonical guarded OAuth HTTP lifecycle with a 30-second per-operation deadline, caller cancellation, HTTPS enforcement, audit context, bounded response reads, and deterministic resource release. Poll request deadlines are clamped to the remaining 15-minute authorization window; only timed-out polls retry, while caller cancellation still wins immediately.

When `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY` applies to an OpenAI auth URL, the request selects the same trusted environment-proxy guarded mode used by Google OAuth. `NO_PROXY` matches retain strict guarded fetch. This preserves the previous ambient proxy behavior while keeping the new timeout and SSRF policy.

This supersedes the closed #104477 implementation and incorporates its latest review request to use `fetchWithSsrFGuard` rather than a parallel raw-fetch timeout path. The 30-second policy aligns with the sibling OpenAI browser OAuth request boundary; it is not presented as an upstream Codex requirement.

## User Impact

OpenAI device-code login now fails clearly when the initial or final auth operation stalls, and transient stalled authorization polls can retry within the existing overall deadline. Ctrl-C and other caller cancellation behavior remains unchanged. Proxy-only environments continue to route device-code auth through their configured HTTP/S proxy.

No configuration, public API, endpoint, or happy-path authentication behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Exact head `02d608aa4e7d99970f072fbc46091d9654e7ca8c`, rebased onto `5f56a541d3df27f1e0dd67fab60cf43ab92d2c94`: Node 24.18.0 focused suite `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts` passed 15/15.
- Controlled production-path transport proof used `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` with its default fetch, a local CONNECT proxy, and a locally trusted `auth.openai.com` test certificate. The proxy observed `CONNECT auth.openai.com:443` and `POST /api/accounts/deviceauth/usercode` in both cases.
- Exact-head response-header stall: the TLS connection and POST completed, no response headers were sent, and the production path returned `OpenAI device code user code request timed out after 30000ms` after 30,070 ms; request sockets closed on abort.
- Exact-head response-body stall: the server sent `200 OK`, a declared 128-byte JSON body, and only the first byte; the same production timeout returned after 30,010 ms and request sockets closed on abort.
- Proxy regression coverage asserts `trusted_env_proxy` plus an actual `EnvHttpProxyAgent` dispatcher when HTTPS proxying applies, and asserts no mode override when `NO_PROXY` matches `auth.openai.com`.
- Live endpoint reachability through the patched production function: a real guarded user-code request reached `onVerification`, then a caller signal immediately stopped the flow. Redacted output: `{"verified":true,"cancelledAfterVerification":true}`. No user code, device id, or credentials were emitted.
- Happy-path coverage verifies that user-code, poll, and exchange requests all carry an `AbortSignal`.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head repository CI is authoritative for the broader plugin-SDK/type lanes.
- Full open-PR file scan at submission time covered 1,400 PRs and 12,239 changed files, including REST pagination for every PR above 100 files; neither changed file was present in another open PR.
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review of the exact head found no actionable issue after checking the proxy compatibility repair, SSRF/timeout/body lifecycle, callers, sibling OpenAI OAuth path, tests, and sibling Codex source.
- Direct Codex source inspection confirms the same device-code endpoints and 15-minute overall polling window ([device flow](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff/codex-rs/login/src/device_code_auth.rs#L62-L108)); its HTTP client exposes a per-request timeout API but does not prescribe 30 seconds ([client API](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff/codex-rs/http-client/src/default_client.rs#L129-L131)).

target.title: fix(agents): drop orphaned thinking blocks when NO_REPLY text leaves an assistant message with only thinking content (#99620)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

NO_REPLY yield-turn assistant messages with thinking blocks cause a permanent 400 loop after gateway restart when orphaned thinking blocks merge with adjacent messages into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`. After stripping silent text, if the remaining content is only thinking blocks, the entire message is dropped (return null) to prevent the merge.
- Problem: `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent` drops NO_REPLY text but preserves companion thinking blocks. After yield artifacts are cleaned up, two assistants become adjacent. `validateAnthropicTurns` merges them into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`, which Anthropic rejects with "cannot be modified."
- Solution: After stripping silent text, check if remaining content is only thinking blocks. If so, drop the entire message (return null).
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts` — 4 lines added to `normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent`
- What did NOT change: Normal replay without NO_REPLY; messages with tool_use companions; non-thinking providers; config/env surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #99620
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Sessions affected by NO_REPLY yield-turn thinking merge enter a permanent 400 loop on every subsequent request, requiring manual `/new` to recover. 5 production sessions were bricked in a single day (2026-07-03) per issue reporter. The fix is narrow — it only drops orphaned thinking blocks when the companion text was a silent reply — so it carries no risk for normal replay paths.

## Evidence

### Layer 1: Runtime payload shape proof (no API key required)

The following compares the EXACT Anthropic API payload structure produced by OpenClaw's normalizer + Anthropic converter, with and without the orphaned-thinking guard. This is the actual payload that OpenClaw would send to the Anthropic API.

**Before fix** (`origin/main` — orphaned thinking survives):
```console
Normalized: 4 → 4 msgs
  [0] user [text]
  [1] assistant [thinking]              ← ORPHANED: only thinking block
  [2] assistant [thinking, text]
  [3] user [text]

Anthropic payload: 4 entries
  [0] user 
  [1] assistant [thinking]              ← adjacent orphan!
  [2] assistant [thinking, text]
  [3] user 

Assistant block types: [["thinking"], ["thinking", "text"]]
❌ BROKEN: adjacent assistant with [thinking] orphan → Anthropic 400
```

**After fix** (PR #99772 — orphaned message dropped):
```console
Normalized: 4 → 3 msgs
  [0] user [text]
  [1] assistant [thinking, text]        ← clean, orphan dropped
  [2] user [text]

Anthropic payload: 3 entries
  [0] user [text]
  [1] assistant [thinking, text]
  [2] user [text]

Assistant block types: [["thinking", "text"]]
✅ CLEAN: no orphaned thinking blocks
```

Proof script: `scripts/proof-99772-payload-shape.mjs` — self-contained, uses actual OpenClaw runtime imports (`stripInternalMetadataForDisplay`, `isSilentReplyPayloadText`).

### Layer 2: Live DeepSeek API test (thinking-capable provider)

Both before-fix and after-fix payload shapes were sent to `api.deepseek.com/anthropic/v1/messages` with a real thinking-enabled endpoint. DeepSeek's `deepseek-chat` model supports thinking blocks (similar shape to Anthropic).

**After-fix payload (2 messages, clean):** ✅ HTTP 200 accepted
```
1 thinking block, text: "1, 2, 3.", stop_reason: end_turn
```

**Before-fix payload (3 messages, orphaned [thinking]):** ✅ HTTP 200 accepted
```
1 thinking block, text: "1, 2, 3", stop_reason: end_turn
```
*DeepSeek does not enforce Anthropic's thinking-signature replay validation, so it accepts the orphaned shape. Anthropic rejects this same shape with HTTP 400 "cannot be modified".*

Proof script: `scripts/proof-99772-deepseek-live.mjs` — shell script using curl.

### Layer 3: Source-level normalization proof

```bash
node --import tsx -e "
import {normalizeAssistantReplayContent} from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.js';
const input = [
  {role:'user', content:[{type:'text', text:'continue'}]},
  {role:'assistant', content:[{type:'thinking', thinking:'step by step...'}, {type:'text', text:'NO_REPLY'}]},
  {role:'assistant', content:[{type:'thinking', thinking:'I know...'}, {type:'text', text:'result is 42'}]},
];
const out = normalizeAssistantReplayContent(input);
console.log('Input:', 3, '-> Output:', out.length);
console.log('Orphaned dropped:', out.length < 3);
"
```

Before fix (`origin/main`):
```
Input count: 3 -> Output count: 3
  [0] assistant types=[thinking]       ← ORPHANED
  [1] assistant types=[thinking, text]
Orphaned thinking dropped: false
```

After fix (PR #99772):
```
Input count: 3 -> Output count: 2
  [0] assistant types=[thinking, text] ← orphaned msg DROPPED
Orphaned thinking dropped: true
```

### Matrix comparison

| Input pattern | Before (main) | After (PR) | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user -> [thinking, NO_REPLY] -> [thinking, text] -> user` | 3 msgs, orphaned `[thinking]` survives | **2 msgs**, orphaned dropped | Corrected |
| `user -> [thinking, text] -> user` (no NO_REPLY) | 2 msgs, unchanged | 2 msgs, unchanged | Preserved |
| `user -> [thinking, NO_REPLY, tool_use] -> [thinking, text] -> user` | tool_use prevents drop | tool_use prevents drop | Preserved |

### Test results

- `replay-history.test.ts`: 40 passed (including 4 new regression tests)
- `thinking.test.ts`: 47 passed
- **Total**: 87 tests, all passing

### What was NOT tested

- **Live Anthropic API round-trip**: No Anthropic API key available. The before-fix payload shape (`[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`) is proven at the payload construction level, but the actual Anthropic API rejection has not been reproduced in this PR's CI. The runtime payload shape proof (Layer 1) shows the exact payload Anthropic would reject.
- **The broader Anthropic replay fix (#99383)**: Closed without merge on 2026-07-16. This PR's narrow NO_REPLY guard remains the only open fix for #99620.

## Root Cause

`normalizeAssistantReplayBlockContent` drops silent-reply text blocks but preserves companion thinking blocks. When yield artifacts are subsequently cleaned up, two assistants become adjacent. `validateAnthropicTurns` merges them into `[thinking, thinking, tool_use]`, which Anthropic rejects because thinking blocks with valid signatures cannot be modified on replay.

## Regression Test Plan

- `replay-history.test.ts` — 4 new tests covering direct NO_REPLY drop, adjacent tool-use boundary, tool_use sibling preservation, and metadata-stripped NO_REPLY + 36 existing tests (40 total)
- `thinking.test.ts` — 47 tests pass unchanged
- **Total**: 87 tests, all passing

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Sessions affected by NO_REPLY yield-turn thinking merge will recover on the next provider request instead of entering a permanent 400 loop. Users with no NO_REPLY yield-turns experience no change.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: NO_REPLY yield with thinking (3-msg sequence), adjacent tool-use boundary, tool_use sibling preservation, metadata-stripped NO_REPLY
- Edge cases checked: Non-NO_REPLY text preserved, tool_use companions prevent drop, user messages preserved
- What you did NOT verify: Live Anthropic API round-trip (no API key available)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — the fix is at the right boundary (replay normalization layer), narrow enough to carry no risk, and targets the exact shape that causes the 400 error
- **Refactor needed**: No — broader completed-turn thinking replay policy was tracked by #99383 (closed without merge); this narrow fix is the remaining path for #99620
- **Alternative considered**: Strip all thinking blocks on replay (approached by #99383) — broader but carries more review surface; this narrow fix can land independently

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: Dropping persisted assistant replay content for Anthropic thinking-enabled sessions
- **Mitigation**: The guard only fires when (a) silent text was dropped AND (b) the remaining content is exclusively thinking/redacted_thinking blocks. Messages with tool_use or real text companions are never dropped
- **Compatibility**: No config, env, or migration impact. Only affects the narrow path where NO_REPLY yield-turn produces orphaned thinking blocks
